task: Task 2 — Real-Browser Keyboard and Accessibility Verification
scope: Characterization only. No production change. Genuine trusted keyboard input via Playwright; assertions read public-observable DOM + the Chromium accessibility tree (CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree). Discrepancies are characterized, never repaired.
t2rNote: This revision is the T2-R corrective. It supersedes the original Task-2 evidence in three material respects: (T2-F01) the Tab-focus test is rebuilt with a correctly-ordered next-tabbable and asserts the actual focus destination — real Tab navigation advances focus normally, so P1.3-D04 is WITHDRAWN; (T2-F02) the D03 observation is preserved and characterized per open path (focus / keyboard-reopen / pointer) without attributing the jsdom discrepancy to a single unproven cause; (T2-F03) the D02 genuine-busy reflection now carries a supported Chromium AX-state assertion (listbox AX `busy`), in addition to the DOM reflection. Reproducibility: certification is pinned to the recorded Chromium build unless an explicit override is supplied.

browser.versionEnforcement: T2-01 asserts the engine version EXACTLY equals the recorded build (156.0.8078.4) for a certification run. If SMILODON_T2_CHROMIUM is set the run is treated as an explicit override run (version recorded, not silently certified).
browser.determinism: single project (chromium), workers=1, fullyParallel=false, retries=0, headless=true

harness.systemUnderTest: vanilla-demo (http://localhost:5173/vanilla-demo.html) with enhanced-select / select-option custom elements; demo's own static selects purged so the AX tree contains only suite-mounted instances
harness.inputModel: Playwright locator.press / focus / click deliver genuine trusted keyboard/pointer events (NOT synthetic event dispatch)
harness.proxyNote: NO_PROXY for localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 is enforced in-config so webServer probes do not traverse the developer outbound proxy
harness.whyChrome1248: The repo pins @playwright/test 1.59.1 whose default Chromium (revision 1217) is geo-blocked on this environment's CDN (HTTP 403). The cache already carries a full Chrome-for-Testing build (chromium-1248) which supports CDP AX tree + ariaSnapshot; Playwright is pointed at it explicitly for reproducibility.

T2-01.title: Browser harness (deterministic Chromium, version recorded & enforced)
findings: Chromium engine version is reported at 156.0.8078.4 and ENFORCED to equal the recorded build for certification; an override is explicitly flagged (T2-R reproducibility).
Mounted combobox renders with role=combobox and aria-expanded=false initially.
Initial mount is closed (no data-open) with no aria-activedescendant.

T2-02.title: Keyboard navigation (Arrow/Home/End/Page/Enter/Space)
findings: ArrowDown on a closed+focused combobox opens it AND pre-activates the first option (aria-activedescendant -> 'a').
ArrowDown/ArrowUp move one selectable step and skip a disabled option (a -> c -> a).
ArrowDown/ArrowUp clamp at the first/last selectable option (no wrap-around).
Home jumps to first selectable (a); End jumps to last selectable (d).
PageDown/PageUp move by 10 selectable options (v0 -> v10; v24 -> v14).
Enter activates the active option and closes; Space activates the pre-active option in the non-searchable default.

T2-03.title: Popup dismissal (Escape/Tab/focus transfer/close chronology)
findings: Escape closes an open popup and sets aria-expanded=false.
Tab from a CLOSED combobox advances focus to the next sequential tabbable (control case): activeElement is the following <button id="after-select">.

Tab from an OPEN combobox closes the popup AND advances focus to the next tabbable (activeElement is the following button, not BODY). This DISPROVES the originally-proposed P1.3-D04 (which rested on a mis-ordered comparison button placed BEFORE the select); P1.3-D04 is WITHDRAWN.
Escape and Tab both emit close with empty detail ({}); indistinguishable — confirms P1.3-D01 in a real browser.
Escape/Tab while already closed emit no close event.

T2-04.title: DOM focus (document.activeElement + shadow root)
findings: DOM focus is on the ENHANCED-SELECT host; the shadow active element is the combobox input (part=input).
Focus stays on the input across open + arrow movement; the active option is expressed via aria-activedescendant, never via DOM focus.
Escape leaves DOM focus on the combobox input.

T2-05.title: ARIA relationships (combobox/listbox/option/aria-controls/expanded/activedescendant)
findings: combobox aria-controls equals the listbox id (aria-owns also present).
aria-expanded reflects open/closed; aria-activedescendant resolves to an option.
AX tree exposes a combobox with hasPopup=listbox and controls, plus >=1 listbox role.

T2-06.title: Disabled options (keyboard exclusion + a11y state)
findings: A disabled option is never activated by keyboard traversal (ArrowUp/Down sweep never lands on 'b').
Disabled option exposes aria-disabled=true in the DOM and disabled=true state in the AX tree ('Bravo').

T2-07.title: Selection policies (single/multi/allowDeselect/maxSelections, keyboard-only)
findings: Single mode: Enter selects the active option and closes.
Multi + allowDeselect: Enter toggles a selection off; multi opens with NO pre-active option.
maxSelections caps keyboard selections (second Enter rejected).
Multi-select listbox exposes aria-multiselectable=true.

T2-08.title: Accessibility representation (Chromium AX tree)
findings: Selected option in multi mode is exposed with AX property selected=true. NOTE: a selected option carries a chip remove affordance so its accessible name is '<label> Remove option' (e.g. 'Alpha Remove option'), not the bare label. This is correct behavior (select-option.ts:427 aria-label='Remove option'); the assertion matches by label prefix.
Combobox accessible name derives from a host aria-label ('Favorite color').
aria-activedescendant is reported as a related-node idref on the combobox AX node.

T2-09.title: Reassessment of P1.3-D01/D02/D03 (+ D04 withdrawal) with browser evidence
findings: D01: public close detail is {} in the browser; Escape and Tab indistinguishable — CONFIRMED.

D02: legacy host aria-busy is inert on the listbox (null) BY DESIGN; genuine busy (public load-more click -> _setBusy(true)) DOES reflect aria-busy='true' onto the listbox DOM AND the Chromium listbox AX node reports busy=true — RESOLVED (reflection target = listbox; works when actually busy; the jsdom 'missing' was the inert legacy attribute, not a defect). The AX busy-state claim is backed by an explicit AX assertion (T2-F03).

D03: opening PRE-ACTIVATES the first selectable option in the browser across all three observable open paths — (a) focus-triggered open, (b) closed-and-focused keyboard reopen (ArrowDown), and (c) pointer open. The browser result is preserved; the discrepancy with Task-1 jsdom is characterized per path and is NOT attributed to a single unproven cause (T2-F02).

D04: WITHDRAWN. With a correctly-ordered next-tabbable, Tab advances focus normally from both the closed and open states; the original BODY result was an end-of-document fallback from a comparison button placed before the select (T2-F01).

T2-10.title: Regression / harness integrity (browser path uses public surface only)
findings: A complete open -> move -> select cycle is driven entirely through real keyboard input on the public surface; no private-method assertion helpers.

P1.3-D01.detail: CloseEventDetail is empty {}; Escape and Tab both emit close:{} in Chromium. No close reason surfaced. Disposition unchanged: characterized, design decision deferred; no production change; no ADR.
P1.3-D01.evidence: T2-03 close-detail tests + T2-09 D01 test

P1.3-D02.browserStatus: RESOLVED (not a defect; DOM + AX verified)
P1.3-D02.detail: The listbox IS the aria-busy reflection target. When genuinely busy (public load-more click -> _setBusy(true)) it receives aria-busy='true' in the DOM, AND the Chromium accessibility tree reports busy=true on the listbox AX node (T2-F03 assertion). The legacy host aria-busy attribute is intentionally inert for listbox semantics (in-code comment in _syncListboxAccessibility). The Task-1 jsdom observation tested the inert legacy attribute, which is NOT a limitation.
sourceReferences: packages/core/src/platform/web/accessibility-effects.ts (applyListbox sets aria-busy on listbox when effect.busy)
packages/core/src/components/enhanced-select.ts _syncListboxAccessibility (~4294) — sets busy only when isBusy || (protocol==='acknowledged' && host aria-busy==='true')
P1.3-D02.recommendation: Resolved at both DOM and AX levels: reflection target is the listbox and it is exposed (DOM aria-busy + AX busy) when genuinely busy. No production change.
P1.3-D02.evidence: T2-09 D02 test (legacy inert + genuine busy DOM reflection + listbox AX busy=true)

P1.3-D03.browserStatus: BROWSER OBSERVATION ACCEPTED; root-cause attribution WITHHELD
P1.3-D03.detail: In Chromium the popup pre-activates the first selectable option (aria-activedescendant -> first) on open. This holds across all three observable open paths — focus-triggered open, closed-and-focused keyboard reopen (ArrowDown), and pointer open. The Task-1 jsdom 'opening assigns no initial aria-activedescendant' result does not reproduce here. The differing focus/open sequences between the jsdom and browser harnesses are NOT attributed to a single unproven cause (T2-F02); the browser result is preserved as the real-browser observation.
P1.3-D03.apgNote: Difference from an APG example is not, by itself, nonconformance. Recorded as observation; no defect asserted.
P1.3-D03.evidence: T2-02 ArrowDown-open test + T2-09 D03 test (all three open paths)

P1.3-D04.priorClass: Observation (proposed in the original Task-2 evidence)
P1.3-D04.detail: The originally-proposed P1.3-D04 ('Tab closes the popup but does not advance DOM focus; activeElement falls back to BODY') was based on a test that appended its comparison button BEFORE the select, so BODY was simply the end-of-document Tab fallback. With a correctly-ordered next-tabbable mounted AFTER the select, Tab advances focus to the next control from both the closed and open states. The deviation is therefore WITHDRAWN; there is no Tab focus-transfer defect to record.
P1.3-D04.evidence: T2-03 'Tab from a closed combobox advances...' (control) and 'Tab from an open combobox closes it AND advances...'

AX-selected-option-name.summary: A selected option in multi mode has an accessible name suffixed with 'Remove option'.
AX-selected-option-name.detail: select-option.ts:427 gives the chip remove button aria-label='Remove option'; the composed option AX name becomes '<label> Remove option'. Selection is exposed via the AX 'selected' property (true). This is correct; the T2-08 assertion matches by label prefix.

T2-F01.problem: The D04 test created its comparison button BEFORE mounting the select and only asserted inequality with that button's id (never that focus was BODY).
T2-F01.fix: Mount the select first, append a genuinely-tabbable <button id="after-select"> AFTER it; add a closed-combobox control case; assert the ACTUAL focus destination (tag+id) is the next button.
T2-F01.outcome: Real Tab advances focus normally in both closed and open states -> P1.3-D04 WITHDRAWN.

T2-F02.problem: Calling the jsdom result an 'artifact' assigned an unproven cause; the focus/open sequences differ between harnesses.
T2-F02.fix: Characterize each open path separately (focus-triggered, closed+focused keyboard reopen, pointer); preserve the browser result; withhold root-cause attribution.
T2-F02.outcome: All three open paths pre-activate the first option in the browser; recorded as a browser observation, not a cause attribution.

T2-F03.problem: The browser test checked the listbox DOM aria-busy, but the evidence additionally claimed Chromium exposes the busy state in the AX tree unbacked by an assertion.
T2-F03.fix: Added a Chromium accessibility-tree assertion: a listbox AX node reports busy=true when genuinely busy (in addition to the DOM aria-busy reflection).
T2-F03.outcome: The AX busy claim is now backed; D02 is verified at both DOM and AX levels.

Reproducibility.summary: Certification pinned to the recorded Chromium build.
Reproducibility.fix: T2-01 now asserts the engine version is EXACTLY the recorded build (156.0.8078.4) for certification; an SMILODON_T2_CHROMIUM run is explicitly flagged as an override run (version recorded, not silently certified).

coverageImplications.P1.3-D02: Diagnostic -> resolved at DOM + AX level (listbox is the reflection target; aria-busy in DOM and busy in AX when genuinely busy). The Task-1 Diagnostic guard remains as a regression pin.
coverageImplications.P1.3-D03: Observation -> browser confirms first-option pre-activation across focus/keyboard/pointer open; root-cause of the jsdom discrepancy withheld. No behavior change.
coverageImplications.P1.3-D01: Confirmed in browser; remains a documented public-contract limitation.
coverageImplications.P1.3-D04: Withdrawn (not added to the deviation register); Tab focus transfer is normal in a real browser.
